text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Court in Mainz acquits 11 adults accused of child sex abuse.
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer will meet this week to discuss revaluation of the bank's currency reserves, finance ministry says.
- IAB labour market institute predicts jobs situation in Germany will deteriorate further this year.
- Metal industry employers and trade unions fail to reach agreement on system of part-time work for older workers.
HANDELSBLATT
- Government likely to revalue gold reserves in year 2000, Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke says.
- Stella AG to be exclusive producer of Wlat Disney musicals in mainland Europe.
- Heiner Geissler, senior member of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), warns party its reputation for economic management has been damaged by row over budget.
- Politicians criticise trip to Iran by Juergen Moellemann, self-styled Middle East expert of liberal Free Democrats (FDP).
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Opposition Greens party wants cut in pensions for civil servants.
- Wolfgang Clement, Economics Minister Germany's most populous state of in North Rhine-Westphalia, says he wants to succeed Johannes Rau as state premier.
- Prosecutors investigate widespread illegal employment practices.
- Customers could soon face higher charges for withdrawing money from a cash machine which does not belong to their own bank.
- German energy companies produced three percent more electricity in 1996 compared to the previous year.
DIE WELT
- Police detain suspect in case of arson attack on a church in the northern town of Husum.
- German medicine manufacturers' producer prices rose by 4.3 percent to 29.7 billion marks in 1996.
- Trade unions and employers in Bavraian retail sector reach wage deal, offering hope similar deals can soon be agreed in other regional states.
